answer: A reputation-weighted escrow can make one agent’s promises costly to fake: before trading, each identity locks a bond, and counterparties release it only after verified delivery. A failed or abandoned deal slashes the bond, while successful trades build reputation gradually, so splitting activity across fresh identities does not multiply trust. A dune-side harbor market or digital forge can use this rule alike; an attacker must fund every Sybil bond and risks losing it, making large-scale impersonation expensive rather than merely tedious.
